title: Japanese Choosing 'Coolcations' for Summer Trips
paragraphs: When you think of a perfect summer vacation, you might picture lazy days on the beach, getting lost in the streets of a new city, or going on a long hike through the countryside.

But it's hard to enjoy any of those things when temperatures climb above 35 degrees Celsius. The beach starts to feel like a frying pan, getting lost becomes a never-ending search for shade, and that hike suddenly looks more like a survival challenge.
That's why more and more people are looking for cooler summer vacations, often called "coolcations."
And they're becoming popular in Japan too.

Travel platform Agoda compared accommodation searches by Japanese travelers for check-ins between April and June with searches for check-ins between July and September. It found that more people were looking at cooler places later in the summer.

Tateshina Highlands in Nagano prefecture saw the biggest jump, with accommodation searches increasing by 277%. Less than a three-hour drive from Tokyo, this mountain area is cooler than many other parts of Japan in summer. It's a good place for long walks, scenic drives and relaxing in hot springs.
Furano in Hokkaido was also popular, with searches up 229%. Visitors can enjoy beautiful flower fields, good food and lots of outdoor activities.

Next on the list was Yuzawa in Niigata prefecture, where searches increased by 202%. Better known as a winter ski destination, Yuzawa is also attracting travelers who want to enjoy the outdoors during the summer months.
Other popular places included Karuizawa and the Matsumoto and Kamikochi area. Both are in Nagano prefecture and offer cooler weather, green mountains and lots of enjoyable ways to spend time outside.
